issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a SealSaloon constructor that takes a String (the saloon name) and implies storing that name, but both the template (Main) and the solution implement and use a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()). This mismatch leaves students unclear whether to implement a no-arg constructor or a constructor accepting a String and whether a saloon name field is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor requirement across artifacts. Either (A) update the template and solution to provide a public SealSaloon(String name) constructor and add a private final String name field with a getter (and update Main to construct with a name), or (B) revise the problem statement and UML to specify a no-argument constructor if the saloon name is not required. Ensure the chosen approach is consistent in the UML, problem text, template Main, and reference solution.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for SealSaloon: the problem statement and UML require a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts the saloon name, but both the template usage (Main) and the provided solution implement and use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). This API mismatch can confuse students about which constructor to implement and how to wire up the class according to the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Either update the solution and template to provide and use a constructor with signature public SealSaloon(String name) (e.g., add public SealSaloon(String name) { this(); /* store name if needed */ }) or modify the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor. The preferred fix is to add public SealSaloon(String name) to the SealSaloon class so it matches the UML and problem description.
